name: Rajasthan
tagline: Pink city, blue city, white city — the royal circuit in colour
hero_description: Rajasthan is India's great heritage road-trip: Jaipur's UNESCO-listed pink grid and mirror-mosaic Amber Fort, Jodhpur's indigo old town under the ramparts of Mehrangarh, and Udaipur's white palaces terraced above Lake Pichola. Push further west and the Thar desert delivers camel-back sunsets at the living fort city of Jaisalmer.
best_time_to_visit: October to March — dry, cool sightseeing weather; desert summers are brutally hot, and forts are best walked first thing in the morning before the ~10 am crowds.

top_attractions.name: Amber Fort, Jaipur
top_attractions.description: Begun in 1592 under Raja Man Singh I as the Kachwaha capital before Jaipur existed — red sandstone and marble courtyards climbing a ridge, crowned by the Sheesh Mahal's thousands of mirror mosaics.

top_attractions.name: Hawa Mahal, Jaipur
top_attractions.description: The 1799 'Palace of Winds' — a five-storey pink facade pierced by 953 jharokha windows, built so royal women could watch street processions unseen.

top_attractions.name: Mehrangarh Fort, Jodhpur
top_attractions.description: Founded around 1459 by Rao Jodha, its ramparts rise roughly 120 m straight from the rock — the view down over Jodhpur's indigo-washed houses is why it's called the Blue City.

top_attractions.name: City Palace, Udaipur
top_attractions.description: Rajasthan's largest palace complex, begun in 1553 under Udai Singh II — a terraced run of courtyards and balconies above Lake Pichola, with the Lake Palace appearing to float mid-lake below.

top_attractions.name: Jaisalmer Fort
top_attractions.description: Raised in 1156 in golden-yellow sandstone, this is one of the world's few living forts — a sizeable share of the old city's residents still live and trade inside its walls.

top_attractions.name: Jaipur's walled old city
top_attractions.description: A planned grid city of 1727, UNESCO World Heritage listed in 2019 — its bazaars still sort by trade: block-print textiles, blue pottery, silver and gemstones street by street.

activities: Sunrise walk through Amber Fort before the tour buses arrive
Bazaar crawl in Jaipur's old city — block prints, blue pottery, gems
Sunset boat ride on Lake Pichola
Rampart walk at Mehrangarh with Blue City rooftop views
Camel safari and dunes sunset at Sam, near Jaisalmer
Rajasthani thali dinner with kalbeliya folk dance and puppetry
Stepwell stop at Panna Meena ka Kund near Amber
A night in a heritage haveli
